claim: Audit 1, Impact: "about 12–30 staff hours a week, roughly $19,000–$47,000 a year ... assuming 150–400 inquiries a month of 6–10 minutes."
problem: The numbers are not derivable from the audit's own assumptions and are roughly twice the maximum they allow. 150–400 inquiries a month at 6–10 minutes is 900–4,000 minutes a month, i.e. 3.5–15.4 staff hours a week and at most 800 hours a year; the audit claims 12–30 hours a week (624–1,560 hours a year). The dollar range is internally consistent with the hours ($47,000 ≈ 1,560 h × $30.33) but those hours do not exist under the stated volume. analysis.json also assumed only 40–60% of intake work is recoverable, which the audit body drops, so even the honest gross range would be about 1.4–9 hours a week. As written, the headline saving is inflated.
fix: Re-derive from the stated assumptions and state the recoverable share: "about 3–15 staff hours a week of intake entry and callback chasing, 40–60% of it recoverable (roughly 1.5–9 hours), about $2,500–$14,000 a year at $30/hour" — or, if 12–30 hours is the intended figure, raise the assumed volume to roughly 300–900 inquiries a month and say so.

claim: Audit 2, Impact: "roughly 450–1,500 staff hours a year ... assuming 150–400 matters at 3–6 chase hours each."
problem: Those assumptions give 450–2,400 hours of gross work, and analysis.json applies a 30–60% automatable share to it. The audit presents 450 hours as a saving, which implies 100% removal of all chase work at the lowest volume, and 1,500 hours is 62.5% of the top volume, above the stated 60% ceiling. The low end is therefore overstated (a 30% share of 450 hours is about 135).
fix: Apply the share explicitly: "roughly 150–1,400 staff hours a year (30–60% of 450–2,400), about $5,000–$48,000 at $34/hour, plan on $15,000–$30,000" — and keep the existing assumption sentence so the reader can reproduce it.

claim: For-the-founder email: "its published office hours stop at 8pm on weekdays".
problem: Only the Manalapan page publishes hours; the New Brunswick and Somerville pages were opened and publish none, which the audit body itself notes. The email states it firm-wide without that qualifier, so a careful reader at the firm could call it inaccurate.
fix: Say "its Manalapan office publishes 8pm weekday hours and no weekend hours" or "the hours it publishes stop at 8pm".

claim: Audit 3, Now: "with no status lookup, every update question is a weekday call".
problem: This is an inference (from the absence of a portal) stated as fact with an absolute "every", and it is odd next to the firm's 24/7 intake line — an after-hours status question reaches whoever answers the phone, not necessarily a weekday paralegal call.
fix: Frame it as inference: "with no status lookup, status questions land on calls to staff during office hours (inference from the absence of any portal or FAQ lookup)", and drop "every".

claim: Audit 2, Now: "...work businesses like yours often absorb into existing paralegals"; Audit 3, Now: "businesses like yours often find that costs per call, not scale".
problem: Unsourced generalisations about how comparable firms operate, presented as fact rather than as the consultancy's own observation. Nothing in the sources establishes what peer firms do.
fix: Mark them plainly: "in our experience at firms this size, paralegals absorb this work" — or cut them; they add length without evidence.

problem: No claim in the body carries an inline pointer to the source list, so a reader cannot tell which of the eight listed URLs supports which statement, and the wage-derived figures cannot be checked without redoing the arithmetic.
fix: Add short inline tags (e.g. "[manalapan]", "[contact]", "[O*NET paralegal]") against each factual sentence, and show the hour→dollar conversion once (e.g. "1,000 h × $34/hr").
